role_in_parent: Handles the first residue class modulo 8 in a self-contained way, avoiding the broken universal counting lemma from the failed attempts.
statement_nl: Let p be a prime number with p > 5 and p ≡ 1 (mod 8). For each k in {1,2,...,p-1}, let I(k) be the unique integer in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), and define S = { k in {1,2,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| >= floor(p/4).

domain_restrictions: p is restricted to prime integers with p > 5 and satisfying the congruence condition p ≡ 1 (mod 8) as written
k is an integer in {1,...,p-1}; when used in S, k is restricted to {1,...,p-2} so that k+1 ∈ {2,...,p-1}
I(k) is the unique representative of k^{-1} modulo p chosen in the set {1,...,p-1}
Comparisons I(k+1) < I(k) are ordinary integer comparisons on these representatives
floor(p/4) denotes the integer floor function of the rational p/4
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every prime p with p > 5 and p ≡ 1 (mod 8) (interpreting the symbol \u2261 here as congruence), define the function I_p: {1,...,p-1} -> {1,...,p-1} by I_p(k) being the unique integer in {1,...,p-1} with k * I_p(k) ≡ 1 (mod p). Let S_p = { k ∈ {1,...,p-2} : I_p(k+1) < I_p(k) }. Then |S_p| ≥ floor(p/4).
quantifier_order: For all primes p with p > 5 and (p ≡ 1 (mod 8)) (interpretation of \u2261 addressed in ambiguities)
For each k in {1,2,...,p-1}, there exists a unique integer I(k) in {1,2,...,p-1} with k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p)
Define S := { k in {1,2,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) } (no further quantification; S is determined by p and I)
Claim: |S| ≥ floor(p/4) (a universal lower bound depending only on p)

variables.name: p
variables.role: parameter (fixed prime for the statement); subject of congruence and inequality conditions

variables.name: k
variables.role: index ranging over residues mod p excluding 0; index for comparing inverses

variables.name: I
variables.role: maps k to the unique multiplicative inverse of k modulo p, represented in the canonical residue set {1,...,p-1}

variables.name: I(k)
variables.role: value of the inverse function at k, satisfies k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p)

variables.name: S
variables.role: set of indices k for which the inverse decreases at the step k->k+1

witness_dependencies: The witness I(k) is dependent on both p and k: I(k) = the multiplicative inverse of k modulo p, chosen in {1,...,p-1}
S depends on p only through the function I (i.e. S = S(p) = {k : I_p(k+1) < I_p(k)})
The numerical bound floor(p/4) depends only on p (not on additional choices), so the existential content is none: claim is a lower bound on |S| for each admissible p
